• people.<domain> is a new core subdomain that routes to the Hub's directory UI/API. It is accessible to any signed-in user (not just administrators).
  • Hub listener. The Hub serves a second HTTP listener on port 8889 (configurable via HUB_PEOPLE_ADDR, default :8889). This listener serves only the directory UI and API (Users, Groups, Org chart, Import), with per-request permission checks. App, policy, drift, compose and Docker endpoints are not registered on this listener.
  • Core routing. Core routes people.<domain> to http://hub:8889 with the middleware chain: rate-limit@file, client-headers@file, portcullis-auth@docker, portcullis-groups@docker, hub-proxy-secret@docker, security-headers@file. The same X-Portcullis-Proxy-Secret header is required.
  • group-gate-map.conf. The map file uses the special value * (asterisk) for the people subdomain, meaning "any signed-in user". This value is valid only in group-gate-map.conf, never in the policy file.
  • Redirect. The existing directory.<domain> subdomain redirects to https://people.<domain>/ (previously it redirected to https://hub.<domain>/#users).

items.title: 6. Docker access
items.text:
Neither Traefik nor the Hub mounts /var/run/docker.sock directly. Each gets its own socket proxy, on its own internal network:

Client Proxy endpoint Allowed Traefik tcp://socket-proxy-traefik:2375 read-only (POST=0): containers, networks, events, version, ping Hub tcp://socket-proxy-hub:2375 containers, images, networks, volumes, exec, events, info, version, ping, logs, plus POST/PUT/DELETE. No build, commit, swarm, nodes, services, tasks, plugins, secrets, configs, system (df/prune), auth, distribution or session

The Hub reads DOCKER_HOST for both the docker compose CLI (only up/down) and its own Engine API calls (status, logs, exec, events). Core CI checks that only the two proxies mount the socket and that each proxy network has exactly its two members. See Security & Hardening.

items.title: 7. Docs ⇄ templates
items.text:
• Generator. scripts/generate-app-docs.py in the docs repo reads every <app-id>/manifest.yaml and writes docs/apps/*.md plus docs/apps/.nav.yml.
  • Triggers.
    • On push to main, the templates repo sends a repository_dispatch event (templates-updated) to the docs repo, which rebuilds the site. This needs the DOCS_DISPATCH_TOKEN secret in the templates repo.
    • The docs repo also rebuilds daily as a fallback.

items.title: 8. Keycloak clients (core ⇄ Hub ⇄ templates)
items.text:
• Client scopes core provides. ./portcullis keycloak configure keeps these realm client scopes in place (idempotent):
    • acr (with an amr mapper) and groups (claim groups, plain group names).
    • email-unverified: protocol openid-connect, included in the token scope, with exactly one mapper, email (user property email → claim email in the ID token, access token, userinfo and introspection). It has no email_verified mapper; any other mapper on the scope is deleted on the next run.

  • What the Hub attaches. A client the Hub creates for a template's keycloak_clients[] entry gets the default client scopes profile, acr, groups and exactly one of the two email scopes; on reconcile the Hub re-attaches acr, groups and that email scope if they are missing:

    • email (the default): tokens carry email and email_verified: false, because LLDAP email is user-editable and the LDAP federation has trustEmail=false.
    • email-unverified, when the entry sets email_verified_claim: false: tokens carry email and no email_verified claim.

    On create and on every reconcile (enable, ACR push), the Hub attaches the wanted one first, then detaches the other one from the client's default and optional scopes. It does this only for clients it may reconcile (owner tag, or an untagged client that points only at the template's hosts; see Hub → Keycloak clients). If the realm has no email-unverified scope, the Hub reports an error and leaves the client's email scope attached. - What the template must do. An app with email_verified_claim: false must not request the email scope: Keycloak answers invalid_scope to a requested scope the client doesn't have. email-unverified is a default scope, so the email claim arrives without being requested. tests/validate.py rejects *SCOPE* environment values that contain email for such templates. - Use it only for apps that refuse email_verified=false but accept it absent (Vaultwarden SSO signups). The email is exactly as unverified as before: identity stays sub / preferred_username (§5), and the app must still never link accounts by email.

items.title: 9. Hub ⇄ LLDAP (users & groups)
items.text: Day-to-day user administration happens in the Hub's Users & Groups tab. The Hub is already behind forward-auth, lldap_admin and WebAuthn step-up; LLDAP's own web UI (0.6.3) has a separate login and no SSO or header auth. It stays available as a fallback.

items.title: 9.1 Service account (core provides)
items.text:
• Account. Core creates an LLDAP user portcullis-hub, makes it a member of lldap_admin, and gives it a random password (≥ 32 characters). It keeps the account in place idempotently on every ./portcullis up: create it if missing, re-add it to lldap_admin, and reset the password if the files and LLDAP disagree.
  • Credentials are files, never env vars. Core mounts them read-only into the Hub as /run/portcullis/lldap/username and /run/portcullis/lldap/password, owned by group 10001 with mode 0640 (directory 0750). The Hub reads them on every LLDAP login, so a rotated password needs no restart. One trailing newline is ignored.

  • Hub configuration.

    Env var (Hub) Default Meaning HUB_LLDAP_CREDENTIALS_DIR /run/portcullis/lldap directory with username and password LLDAP_HTTP_URL http://lldap:17170 LLDAP HTTP API LLDAP_LDAP_URL ldap://lldap:3890 LLDAP LDAP, used only to set passwords (ldaps:// also accepted) LLDAP_BASE_DN dc=portcullis,dc=local must equal LLDAP's LLDAP_LDAP_BASE_DN (core: ${LLDAP_BASE_DN})

  • Not configured. If the files are missing, empty, or the username isn't a valid username, the Users & Groups tab shows "user management is disabled" and why. Every /api/directory mutation answers 503, and the rest of the Hub works as before.

  • Network. The Hub reaches lldap:17170 and lldap:3890 on the portcullis network, the same way Keycloak's LDAP federation and enroll do.
  • Why lldap_admin. LLDAP 0.6.3's narrower lldap_password_manager can only change passwords of non-admins: createUser, createGroup, addUserToGroup, deleteUser and the other GraphQL mutations go through get_admin_handler, which requires Permission::Admin (crates/graphql-server/src/mutation/mod.rs, crates/access-control/src/lib.rs).
  • Contained. The account can never sign in through the gateway: Keycloak's LDAP federation has the user filter (!(uid=portcullis-hub)), so it is never imported (keycloak configure also deletes a copy imported earlier), and group-gate denies the username portcullis-hub on every endpoint (GATE_DENY_USERS).
  • Why this is acceptable. lldap_admin can put anyone into lldap_admin. The Hub could already start arbitrary containers through its socket proxy (§6), so it is host-root-equivalent anyway. Every change it makes is attributed to the signed-in admin and audited (§9.5).

items.title: 9.2 What the Hub calls
items.text:
• Login. POST /auth/simple/login {"username","password"} returns {token, refreshToken}. The JWT is cached until one minute before its exp. On expiry or on a 401, the Hub tries GET /auth/refresh with the Refresh-Token header first, then logs in again.
  • GraphQL (POST /api/graphql, Authorization: Bearer <jwt>). The Hub uses only these operations: users { id email displayName creationDate groups { id displayName } }, groups { id displayName creationDate users { id } }, createUser, updateUser (email, displayName), deleteUser, createGroup, deleteGroup, addUserToGroup, removeUserFromGroup.

  • Passwords: LDAP Password Modify (RFC 3062), not HTTP. LLDAP stores passwords with OPAQUE. Its HTTP endpoints (/auth/opaque/register/start|finish) expect the client half of the OPAQUE registration (ristretto255 + argon2), which the Go standard library can't do. LLDAP 0.6.3 has no GraphQL password mutation. Its LDAP server, however, implements the Password Modify extended operation (1.3.6.1.4.1.4203.1.11.1) and runs the OPAQUE registration server-side (crates/ldap/src/password.rs; lldap_admin may change any password). So the Hub:

    1. simple-binds as uid=portcullis-hub,ou=people,<base DN>;
    2. sends userIdentity = uid=<user>,ou=people,<base DN> and newPasswd;
    3. unbinds.

    The password crosses the internal portcullis network in clear text, like Keycloak's and enroll's LDAP binds today. Core may switch to LDAPS by setting LLDAP_LDAP_URL=ldaps://….

items.title: 9.3 Keycloak side
items.text:
• LDAP users are imported into Keycloak lazily. The Hub uses its existing Keycloak admin credentials (KEYCLOAK_ADMIN, KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD) and imports a user explicitly with GET /admin/realms/portcullis/users?username=<u>&exact=true, which makes the LDAP federation import the user.
  • Status shown. The Hub shows whether a user is imported, their WebAuthn credential count (webauthn + webauthn-passwordless) and their pending required actions. It doesn't show client certificates: they live in Vault/enroll, not in Keycloak.
  • Status lookups. The Hub lists users (GET …/users?max=1000&briefRepresentation=false) and the realm's LDAP provider (GET …/components?type=org.keycloak.storage.UserStorageProvider, providerId ldap), then reads GET …/users/{id}/credentials per user. A failed credentials lookup marks only that user.
  • Stale records. A Keycloak user whose federationLink is the LDAP provider but whose username isn't in LLDAP is listed as stale. The Hub deletes such a copy by id only on an explicit, confirmed request. Never for admin, the service account, users LLDAP has, or Keycloak-local users.
  • Remove passkeys. Deletes every WebAuthn credential, signs the user out (POST …/users/{id}/logout), then either requests a new invite (§9.4) or, for password users, adds webauthn-register-passwordless.
  • Password reset. Signs the user out of Keycloak.
  • Delete. The Hub deletes the user in LLDAP, then deletes the Keycloak copy by id. The federation is READ_ONLY, so this never writes to LDAP.
  • No other changes. The Hub doesn't touch the federation's settings or its built-in mappers (it adds only its own portcullis-attr-<field> mappers, §9.6). Core sets the federation's cachePolicy to NO_CACHE (realm export and ./portcullis keycloak configure), so LLDAP group and attribute changes reach the next token.

items.title: 9.4 One-time invites (core provides)
items.text:
New users are onboarded without a password. The admin creates the user in the Hub and gets a one-time link. The user opens it, registers their security key, and is signed in. There are no other manual steps.

  • Endpoint. Core (enroll) serves POST /internal/invites on a listener that Traefik does not route: http://enroll:8444, the portcullis network only.
    • Hub configuration: HUB_INVITE_API_URL (default http://enroll:8444/internal/invites).
    • Shared secret: a file of ≥ 32 characters, mounted read-only into both containers. In the Hub it is at HUB_INVITE_SECRET_FILE (default /run/portcullis/invite/secret, group 10001, 0640). Never an env var. Core keeps it in secrets/enroll/invite-api-secret (enroll) and secrets/hub/invite/secret (Hub), generated by ./portcullis up.
  • Request. Authorization: Bearer <secret>, Content-Type: application/json, body {"username": "<lldap user id>"}.
  • Response. 201 with {"url": "https://enroll.<domain>/invite/<token>", "expires_at": "<RFC 3339>"}. The Hub accepts only https URLs with a host and no userinfo, and requires expires_at.
  • Errors. Non-2xx with an optional {"error": "<message>"}, which the Hub shows to the admin (truncated to 200 characters). Suggested codes:
    • 401/403: wrong secret;
    • 404: no such LLDAP user;
    • 409: refused, e.g. a protected account.
  • Semantics (core).
    • The token is random (256 bit), stored only as a hash, single-use and expires after 72 h. Invites live in enroll's memory: restarting enroll invalidates pending ones (issue a new invite).
    • Creating an invite revokes the user's earlier unredeemed invites. A user who already has keys gets one more (core's login theme gives every new passkey a unique label); to replace lost keys, delete them first (the Hub's "Reset passkeys", or ./portcullis invite <user> --replace-keys).
    • Opening the link (GET) does not use it; the page's same-origin POST does. Redeeming adds webauthn-register-passwordless to the Keycloak user (enroll's service account portcullis-enroll), signs the user in through the hidden Keycloak identity provider portcullis-invite (first login links the existing LLDAP user, never creates one), requires the passkey registration, and lands on https://<domain>/ (the portal). The session has acr=hwk, amr=[hwk].
    • Core's API refuses (409) portcullis-hub, admin and every member of lldap_admin, lldap_password_manager, the groups of the core subdomains in group-gate-map.conf and INVITE_PROTECTED_GROUPS: an invite hands the account to whoever holds the link, so the API secret must not be a way to take over an administrator. It looks the groups up in LLDAP and fails closed (503) when it can't. For invites made through this API the check is repeated when the link is redeemed and again in the identity-provider steps (authorization code, token): a user added to a protected group after the invite was created gets a "no longer usable" page, and their pending API invites are cancelled. Administrators are invited / recovered only from the server (./portcullis invite <user>, a loopback listener reached through docker exec), never through the Hub.
    • Sign-in has no password: the browser flow is passkey / client cert only. A password set through the Hub's fallback works for LLDAP's own UI and LDAP-binding apps, not for Keycloak.
  • What the Hub does.
    • New user (invite mode, the default). LLDAP createUser with no password, group memberships, pre-import into Keycloak, then POST /internal/invites. The Hub sets no required action: the invite registers the key. If the invite secret is missing, the Hub refuses invite-mode creation before creating anything.
    • "Send new invite" on any user except portcullis-hub, admin and administrators.
    • "Reset passkeys". Removes the passkeys (§9.3), then sends a new invite (administrators: none, see below).
    • Administrators. The Hub computes the same administrator set as core: lldap_admin, lldap_password_manager, INVITE_PROTECTED_GROUPS (Hub env, same value as enroll's), and the groups of the core subdomains in group-gate-map.conf (Hub: HUB_GATE_MAP_FILE, default $PROJECT_DIR/group-gate/group-gate-map.conf, re-read on use).
      • It never sends invite requests for administrators. "Reset passkeys" for them skips the invite and checks this before removing anything.
      • A new user created into an administrator group is created without an invite. The Hub shows ./portcullis invite <user> instead.
      • A 409 from core is shown as "administrators are recovered from the server: ./portcullis invite <user>", prefixed with core's error text if any.
    • Never stored. The link is shown to the admin once (copy button). The Hub doesn't store it, log it or put it in the audit log.
  • Password fallback. Off by default, under "Advanced". The Hub generates a 26-character random password, shown once, or the admin types one (12 to 256 characters). Optionally it adds webauthn-register-passwordless. The same fallback exists as "Password…" on existing users.

items.title: 9.5 Guardrails and audit (Hub)
items.text:
• Protected accounts. portcullis-hub (the account named in the username file) and admin (core's LLDAP_LDAP_USER_DN; Keycloak's federation and enroll bind as it with LLDAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD) can't be changed through the Hub at all: no delete, edit, password, invite, passkey action or group change. An invite or passkey reset for admin would hand the root account to whoever gets the link, so the bootstrap admin is recovered from the server only (./portcullis invite admin). The Hub's tests check that every user-targeting operation refuses both accounts.
  • Another administrator. An invite, a passkey reset or a password for another lldap_admin member hands the acting admin that account. Core refuses invites for administrators (§9.4): the Hub doesn't offer them and shows "administrators are recovered from the server: ./portcullis invite <user>". A passkey reset or a password for another administrator is allowed only with the target's username typed again ({"confirm": "<username>"}; without it the Hub answers 400), and the audit entry carries target_is_lldap_admin=true.
  • Reserved names. admin and portcullis-hub can't be created. Usernames must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$, stricter than LLDAP, because they end up in DNs and URLs. Group names must match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,127}$, must not start with lldap_, and must not duplicate an existing group (case-insensitive). LLDAP's built-in groups can't be deleted.
  • Self-protection. You can't delete yourself (X-Forwarded-User) or remove yourself from lldap_admin.
  • Last admin. The last remaining human lldap_admin member (every member except portcullis-hub) can't be deleted or removed from lldap_admin.
  • Confirmation. Deleting a user or a group and removing passkeys require the name typed again ({"confirm": "<name>"}).
  • Request guards. Mutations are POST/PUT/DELETE under /api/directory/, behind the proxy secret (§5) and the CSRF guard (same origin, JSON body). Mutations without X-Forwarded-User are refused (403). Checks and changes are serialised.

  • Audit. Every mutation, including refused and failed ones, is appended to $HUB_DATA_DIR/audit.jsonl (mode 0600) as one JSON object per line:

    {"time","actor","action","target","detail","result","error"}

    result is ok, refused or error. The log never contains passwords, tokens or invite links. GET /api/directory/audit and the UI show the last 100 entries.

items.title: 9.6 Custom fields and delegated permissions (NEW)
items.text: Portcullis now supports custom user fields (e.g., department, manager, cost center), rule-based groups (membership computed from field values), and delegated permissions (allowing non-admins to manage people).

items.title: Custom fields
items.text:
• Storage. Custom fields are LLDAP user attributes created by the Hub using LLDAP's schema API (addUserAttribute). Each field has:
    • Type: STRING (LLDAP 0.6.3 limitation)
    • Flags: visible=true, editable=false (users cannot edit their own fields through LLDAP's UI)
  • Field types (Hub-managed):
    • Free text: arbitrary string values
    • List: predefined values the admin maintains
    • Person: references another user by username (e.g., manager field for org charts)
  • Field flags (per field):
    • ShareWithApps (default on): field values are sent to apps as OIDC claims and identity headers (§4.1, §5)
    • Admin-only: only administrators may edit this field (security rule: see below)
  • Visibility. Everyone signed in can see everyone's field values and the org chart.

Example field definitions in directory.yaml:

fields:
  - name: department
    type: list
    share_with_apps: true
    admin_only: false
    list_values:
      - Engineering
      - HR
      - Operations
  - name: manager
    type: person
    share_with_apps: true
    admin_only: false
  - name: security_clearance
    type: list
    share_with_apps: false
    admin_only: true
    list_values:
      - Public
      - Confidential
      - Secret

items.title: Rule-based groups
items.text:
• Group types. A group is either manual (membership managed by hand) or rule-based (membership computed from field values by the Hub).
  • Rules. A rule combines conditions with all/any blocks (nestable). Conditions: is, is not, is one of, is empty, and for person fields, reports to (directly or indirectly).
  • Exceptions. On a rule-based group, a person can be added (although they don't match) or kept out (although they match). Every exception requires a written reason, which is stored and shown.
  • Expiry. Any membership (exceptions, and members of manual groups too) can have an expiry date/time. When a membership expires, the person is removed automatically, and the Hub writes the expiry into the policy file's expiring array (§4) so group-gate enforces it strictly.
  • Reconciliation. The Hub writes computed membership into the real LLDAP groups. group-gate, Keycloak and apps treat rule-based groups exactly like manual groups. Re-evaluation happens on every detail change, rule change, import, exception change, and periodically at most every 60 seconds (binding). group-gate enforces expiring entries exactly regardless of the Hub's reconcile cadence.
  • Audit. Every membership change from rules, expiry or import is audited with its cause.

Example rule (conceptual; stored in directory.yaml):

groups:
  - name: nextcloud_milan
    type: rule
    rule:
      all:
        - field: office_location
          op: is
          value: Milan
        - field: department
          op: is_one_of
          values: [Engineering, Operations]
    exceptions:
      - user: jsmith
        mode: added
        reason: "Contractor working with Milan team"
        added_by: admin
        added_at: "2026-11-01T10:00:00Z"

items.title: Hub-private state: directory.yaml
items.text:
The Hub stores field definitions, rules, exceptions, expiries and permission grants in directory.yaml under $HUB_DATA_DIR. This file is:

  • Atomic (like state.yaml): corrupt file = refuse to start.
  • Never exposed to clients or other repos.
  • LLDAP holds only: user attribute schemas (name, type, flags) and current values; group membership (reconciled by the Hub for rule-based groups).

items.title: Delegated permissions
items.text:
Three permissions can be granted to groups (manual or rule-based):

  1. edit_details: edit user fields, bulk import (CSV review + apply)
  2. invite: create new users via invite link (with no group memberships)

  3. remove: delete users

  4. Grants. Each permission is granted to an LLDAP group the admin picks. Members of that group (non-admins) get the permission. Admins always have all permissions.

  5. Scope. Delegation is global for now (all users, subject to the constraints below). Scoped delegation (e.g., "HR Milan edits only Milan people") is a non-goal for this release.
  6. Protected targets. Delegates may never target:
    • Themselves (X-Forwarded-User)
    • The service account (portcullis-hub)
    • The bootstrap admin
    • Any member of lldap_admin, lldap_password_manager, INVITE_PROTECTED_GROUPS, or the core-subdomain groups in group-gate-map.conf
    • Any member of a permission group
  7. Delegate invite constraints:
    • A delegate's invite creates a user with no groups and no password. The new account is marked created_by: <delegate username>.
    • With edit_details, delegates can fill in fields, making the person match rules. This is visible: the audit records the inviter, and rule memberships show "via rule, account created by X".
    • Delegates can re-invite (send a new invite link) only accounts they created (created_by matches) that still have zero Keycloak credentials (no passkeys, no password). An admin taking over an account (setting a password, resetting passkeys, or sending an invite) clears created_by, so delegates can no longer re-invite it.
  8. Manual groups, exceptions, expiries. Delegates may not modify membership of manual groups, add exceptions, or set expiries. These are admin-only.
  9. Security rules:
    • Rules of protected groups (lldap_admin, lldap_password_manager, INVITE_PROTECTED_GROUPS, core-subdomain groups), permission groups, and app admin groups (admin_group, path_groups admin access) may only reference admin-only fields. A field used by such a rule cannot lose its admin-only flag.
    • A rule of such a group must also not match a person with no field values (every new account): refused with 409.
    • The evaluator never adds an account still marked created_by (a delegate created it, no admin has acted on it since) to such a group; it reports it instead.
    • Built-in groups (lldap_admin, lldap_password_manager, INVITE_PROTECTED_GROUPS, core-subdomain groups) can never be rule-based.
  10. Deleting a group deletes it in LLDAP first, then removes its rule, exceptions, expiries, grace entries and permission grants from directory.yaml; creating a group purges any leftovers for that name first. A re-created group inherits nothing.

Example permissions in directory.yaml:

permissions:
  edit_details:
    granted_to: hr_team
  invite:
    granted_to: hr_team
  remove:
    granted_to: hr_managers

items.title: Fields reach apps
items.text:
• Native-OIDC apps: The Hub creates a Keycloak client scope portcullis-attributes with LDAP attribute mappers and protocol mappers for each shared field. Each field becomes a claim attr_<field> (e.g., attr_department) in access tokens, ID tokens and userinfo. The scope is a default client scope on Hub-registered clients (always included).
  • Forward-auth and header-auth apps: The Hub writes user-attributes.json (§4.1); group-gate returns X-Forwarded-Attr-<Header-Name> headers (§5); the portcullis-groups middleware forwards them.

items.title: 10. Landing portal app list (Hub → core)
items.text:
• File. The Hub writes portal-apps.json atomically into hub_data (/data, next to group-gate-policy.json, mode 0644) whenever it writes the policy file (enable, disable, template sync, settings). A core landing portal reads it like group-gate reads the policy file: mount hub_data read-only.
  • Endpoint. GET /api/portal/apps returns the same document, behind the proxy secret like every other Hub route.

  • Format, version 1.

    {
  "version": 1,
  "apps": [
    {
      "id": "immich",
      "name": "Immich",
      "description": "…",
      "icon": "📷",
      "category": "media",
      "urls": [{"label": "Photos", "url": "https://photos.example.org"}],
      "auth_method": "native-oidc",
      "access_group": "users_immich",
      "admin_group": "admin_immich"
    }
  ]
}
    • Only enabled apps whose template is present are listed, sorted by id.
    • {{DOMAIN}} in URLs is already expanded.
    • access_group is the group group-gate requires (auth.group_access); "" means any signed-in user.
    • admin_group is informational.
    • Rendering. The portal filters by the signed-in user's groups (X-Auth-Request-Groups) and must escape every field. An unknown version means: show nothing.
    • Core's portal is group-gate's /portal at https://<domain>/ (router portal: forward-auth, then replacePath). It reads /hub-data/portal-apps.json, shows only https URLs on the domain, and adds the Hub, the Keycloak realm console, enrollment, LLDAP and Traefik for lldap_admin, plus every user's passkeys (account console) and certificate (enroll.<domain>/self).

items.title: Manifest Reference
items.text:
Every app template has a manifest.yaml that describes the app to the Hub. This page documents every field of the schema.

The authoritative definition is the JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) schema/manifest.schema.json in the templates repo. The Hub enforces the same rules and skips templates that fail them (see Integration Contracts §3). Rules that need the compose file, the filesystem or several templates at once are checked by tests/validate.py (see Validation).

For editor completion, start the manifest with:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=../schema/manifest.schema.json

items.title: Conventions
items.text:
Several types recur throughout the schema:

Type Rule single line A string without control characters (U+0000–U+001F, U+007F) env key ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,127}$. It becomes a key in the per-app .env group An LLDAP group name: ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,63}$ service A service name from the template's compose.yml: ^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]*$ {{DOMAIN}} In urls and redirect URIs, replaced with PORTCULLIS_DOMAIN

No other keys are allowed. Every object in the schema sets additionalProperties: false, so a typo is an error, not a silently ignored field.

items.title: Top-level fields
items.text:
Field Type Required Description name single line, 1–64 chars Yes Display name shown in the Hub description single line, 1–200 chars Yes One-line description of what the app does icon single line, 1–16 chars Yes Unicode emoji for the app card, e.g. "\U0001F4CA" category ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$ Yes Catalog category tags list of unique strings ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.+-]{0,31}$ Yes Searchable tags (lowercase) auth object Yes See auth settings list No See settings ports list No See ports env list No See env keycloak_clients list No; required (at least one) for native-oidc See keycloak_clients config_files list No See config_files urls list No See urls

Categories in use: monitoring, media, productivity, security, networking, ai, devops, finance, vpn, remote-access, public.

items.title: auth
items.text:
Field Type Required Description method enum Yes native-oidc, forward-auth, header-auth, mtls, custom or public (see below) sso true, false or "partial" Yes Whether single sign-on is supported group_access boolean Yes group-gate restricts the app's subdomains to access_group. For custom apps only while Portcullis sign-in is in front of them (native_login) group_admin boolean Yes The app maps admin_group to its admin role access_group group If group_access: true LLDAP group required for access, by convention users_<app> admin_group group If group_admin: true or admin_paths is non-empty LLDAP group for admin privileges, by convention admin_<app> admin_paths list of path prefixes No Paths that additionally require admin_group (see below) public_access object No Public path exceptions: share-link paths the Hub can open without forward-auth (see auth.public_access) native_login object No The app has its own login and no SSO (method: custom only); enables the Hub's Sign-in setting (see auth.native_login) identity_headers list of header names If method: header-auth and public_access is set Headers the app reads the user from (e.g. X-Forwarded-User); the Hub strips them on public paths notes string No Free-text notes about the auth integration. Shown on the app's docs page. Upgrade constraints go here too

Constraints the schema enforces:

  • group_access: true requires access_group.
  • group_admin: true requires admin_group.
  • A non-empty admin_paths requires admin_group.
  • method: public requires group_access: false and an empty (or missing) admin_paths.
  • public_access is only allowed with method forward-auth, header-auth or native-oidc; with header-auth it requires a non-empty identity_headers (each ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,63}$, unique).
  • native_login requires method: custom and sso: false.

access_group is only enforced by group-gate when group_access: true. Otherwise it is informational.

items.title: Auth methods
items.text:
method Meaning Router middlewares native-oidc The app talks OIDC to Keycloak itself. Needs keycloak_clients No portcullis-auth on the host-wide router. Login or admin paths may use a separate PathPrefix router with forward-auth forward-auth oauth2-proxy + group-gate in front. The app has its own login, or none portcullis-auth@docker,portcullis-groups@docker header-auth Forward-auth, and the app also trusts X-Forwarded-User from Traefik (and only from Traefik) portcullis-auth@docker,portcullis-groups@docker mtls Client certificate at the TLS layer tls.options: protected@file, no forward-auth custom The app handles its own sign-in (app-specific account system, e.g. plex.tv). With native_login, the Hub can put Portcullis sign-in in front of it None: the Hub's override adds the gateway pair for Portcullis sign-in public No authentication None

See Choosing an auth method in the templates repo's contributing guide.

items.title: SSO values
items.text:
• true: the user authenticates once in Keycloak and is logged into the app automatically.
  • false: the app has its own login form. Forward-auth only gates access, and the user logs in again.
  • "partial": the app auto-creates users from the identity, but needs extra setup, e.g. role assignment.

items.title: auth.native_login
items.text:
For a custom app that has its own login and no SSO. The Hub then shows a per-app Sign-in setting and implements it with compose-override labels; the template itself never changes.

auth:
  method: custom
  sso: false
  group_access: true          # enforced only behind Portcullis sign-in
  access_group: users_plex
  group_admin: false
  native_login:
    supported: true
    allow_without_gateway: true
    note: Plex signs users in with plex.tv accounts; its TV and mobile apps need "App's own login only".
Field Type Required Description supported true Yes The app's own login protects it on its own allow_without_gateway boolean No (default false) Admins may choose App's own login only (no Portcullis) note string (≤ 500) No Shown next to the Sign-in setting: what the app's login is, what breaks behind forward-auth

The two modes (Apps with their own login):

  • Portcullis sign-in, then the app's own login (default): every router gets portcullis-auth@docker,portcullis-groups@docker in front of its own middlewares, the TLS tier from the policy, and group-gate requires access_group if group_access: true. The access policy applies as for forward-auth.
  • App's own login only (only with allow_without_gateway: true): the template's middlewares without the gateway pair, public@file, no group.

Rules (schema and tests/validate.py; the Hub checks the first two too):

  • only with method: custom and sso: false: an app with SSO is signed in through Portcullis and never gets a way around it;
  • supported must be true (omit the block otherwise);
  • a custom app with group_access: true needs native_login (group-gate only runs behind Portcullis sign-in);
  • the compose file of a custom app never uses portcullis-auth@docker or portcullis-groups@docker: the Hub adds them.

items.title: admin_paths
items.text:
admin_paths lists path prefixes on the app's subdomains that need admin_group in addition to the subdomain's group. The Hub publishes them as group-gate path_groups (see Groups → Path rules).

Each item must:

  • match ^/[A-Za-z0-9._~%!$&'()*+,;=:@/-]*$, be at most 256 characters, and be unique in the list
  • not contain .. or //, and have no . segment (/./, a trailing /.)

Matching is a segment-boundary prefix match: /admin matches /admin and /admin/x, but not /administrator.

Path rules only take effect on routers that use portcullis-groups@docker. validate.py therefore fails if no router with portcullis-auth@docker,portcullis-groups@docker serves each listed path.

auth:
  method: native-oidc
  sso: true
  group_access: true
  group_admin: false
  access_group: users_vaultwarden
  admin_group: admin_vaultwarden
  admin_paths: ["/admin"]

items.title: auth.public_access
items.text:
Public path exceptions let anonymous visitors use an app's share links (Nextcloud /s/<token>, Grafana shared dashboards) while the rest of the host stays behind Portcullis. The template only declares the paths. When an admin turns the exception on in the Hub, the Hub adds one Traefik router for them without forward-auth and group-gate (contracts §3). A template must never ship such a router in compose.yml. The app's own auth (share token, share password, expiry) is all that protects these paths; see Auth policies → Public exceptions.

Field Type Required Description enabled_by_default boolean No (default false) State of the Hub toggle until an admin chooses description string, one line, ≤ 500 No Shown in the Hub above the warning default_mode listed or all No listed: only shares an admin lists in the Hub; all: every share. Default listed if a path has {token}, else all. listed needs a {token} path token_pattern anchored regex ^...$, ≤ 200 If a path has {token} (and only then) Every listed share token must match it credential_headers list of header names No Headers besides Authorization / Proxy-Authorization (always refused) the app logs a user in with, e.g. Immich x-api-key credential_cookies list of cookie names No Cookies the app logs a user in with (session, remember-me, render keys) credential_query list of parameter names No Query parameters the app logs a user in with (e.g. Immich apiKey, Grafana auth_token) static_extensions list of [a-z0-9]{1,8} No Extra file extensions supporting paths may serve (default: avif css eot gif ico jpeg jpg js map mjs otf png svg ttf webp woff woff2). Script extensions (php, phtml, cgi, py, jsp, …) are refused service compose service No Service the public router targets. Default: the only service with HTTP routers paths list, 1–20 Yes See below

Each paths item:

Field Type Required Description prefix path Yes Segment-boundary prefix: /s matches /s and /s/..., not /sx. Letters, digits and . _ ~ - per segment, optional trailing /; one whole segment may be {token}. Not / itself; no wildcards, .., //, %, ?, #, $, quotes or backticks description string, one line, ≤ 200 Yes What the path is for (shown in the Hub and on the app page) supporting boolean No Token-free path the share page needs. Opened in both modes, and only for static files below it unless exact. Can't have {token} exact boolean No Opens only this path itself (Path, no subpaths): a single app route or file the page needs. Requires justification; can't have {token}. A path on the broad list (an exact /index.php is still the whole front controller) also needs broad: true broad boolean No Acknowledges a prefix on the broad list; requires justification justification string If broad: true or exact: true Why the broad prefix / exact route is needed

What each mode opens:

Path kind Mode listed Mode all {token} path, e.g. /s/{token} /s/<t> for each listed token <t> /s (up to the segment before {token}) supporting: true static files under the prefix (see below) same supporting: true + exact: true the exact path same other token-free paths no segment-boundary prefix (or the exact path with exact: true)

Static files means Traefik's PathRegexp of the prefix, dot-free directory segments and a file name ending in a static extension, e.g. /dist/core-common.js or /core/img/actions/a.svg, but not /dist/, /dist/a, /dist/a.php or /dist/x.php/a.js. An app route that only accepts extension-less paths is therefore never reached through a supporting path.

Logins never ride the public router: core's public guard (contracts §5) answers 403 to requests carrying Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, a credential_headers header, a credential_cookies cookie or a credential_query parameter. Cookie and query names are compared case-insensitively after PHP's name mangling (leading spaces dropped, and . become _, name[…] is name), raw and percent-decoded. List every way the app authenticates a request at the pinned version.

In mode listed with no listed share, nothing is opened and no router is generated.

Rules (schema, tests/validate.py and the Hub):

  • Broad prefixes need broad: true and a justification: /api, /apps, /index.php, /ocs, /ocs/v1.php, /ocs/v2.php, /remote.php, /remote.php/dav, /remote.php/webdav, /public.php, /dav, /webdav, /graphql, /rest, /v1, /v2, /v3, /auth, /login, /user, /users, /account, /settings, /identity, /sso, /oidc, and any bare /<name>.php. A {token} path is checked on its mode-all extent (/api/{token} is broad).
  • Never public: anything overlapping /oauth2, /admin or /.well-known, or the app's admin_paths.
  • No overlap with other routers: a prefix (mode-all extent) may not overlap a Path/PathPrefix of another router on the app's hosts (login gates, admin routers, API splits). Traefik's PathPrefix is a plain string prefix, so PathPrefix(/login) overlaps /logins.
  • Analysable routing only: routers on the app's hosts may use only Host, Path, PathPrefix, Method, Header, HeaderRegexp, Query, QueryRegexp and ClientIP, without negation. PathRegexp, negated matchers or unknown matchers make the Hub refuse the template's public plan (it can't prove there is no overlap).
  • token_pattern must be anchored and compile, and must reject "", ., .., a/b, /, backticks, spaces, %2F, ${X}, ) and newlines. The Hub additionally requires tokens of [A-Za-z0-9._~-]{1,128}.
  • Routing names: routers and middlewares named portcullis-public-* are reserved for the Hub.

  • Service: with several routed services, set service. If it defines several Traefik services, exactly one host-wide router on it must name one.

  • Supporting prefixes are directories: a supporting prefix whose last segment looks like a file (/custom.css) must be exact.

Set enabled_by_default: true only when turning the exception on opens nothing by itself (mode listed) and can't weaken the host. Example (Nextcloud, abridged):

auth:
  method: forward-auth
  public_access:
    enabled_by_default: true
    default_mode: listed
    description: Public share links for people without a Portcullis account.
    token_pattern: '^[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,32}$'
    credential_cookies: [nc_username, nc_token, nc_session_id]
    paths:
      - prefix: "/s/{token}"          # quote: { } in flow style is YAML syntax
        description: Share page, password form, download and direct preview
      - prefix: "/public.php/dav/files/{token}"
        description: Public WebDAV of the share
      - prefix: /dist
        description: Compiled JS/CSS
        supporting: true                # static files only
      - prefix: /core/mimeicon
        description: File-type icon for files without a preview
        supporting: true
        exact: true
        justification: "#[PublicPage] route that only redirects to a static icon"
      - prefix: /apps/text/public
        description: Markdown viewer sessions (token in the body, so only in mode all)

items.title: settings
items.text:
User-configurable settings shown in the Hub. Each key becomes a key in the per-app .env.

Field Type Required Description key env key Yes Variable name label single line, non-empty Yes Label shown in the Hub type enum Yes text, path, paths, boolean or select description string No Help text required boolean No The setting must be filled in default string without control chars No Default value options list of strings without control chars Required (at least one) for select The choices of a select target object No Bind-mount target for path / paths (see below)

items.title: Setting types
items.text:
Type Input Example text Free-form text API keys, custom names path One host directory /mnt/media/movies paths Several host directories Several media folders boolean On/off toggle Feature flags select Dropdown of options Log level

options is a list of plain strings. Each string is both the stored value and the label:

settings:
  - key: MYAPP_LOG_LEVEL
    label: Log level
    type: select
    options: [info, debug, warn]
    default: info

items.title: target
items.text:
For path and paths, target says where the host path is mounted:

Field Type Required Description service service Yes Compose service to mount into mount ^/[^:]*$ (absolute, no :, no control chars) Yes Container path 
settings:
  - key: JELLYFIN_MOVIES_PATH
    label: Movies folder
    description: Host path to your movies library
    type: path
    target:
      service: jellyfin
      mount: /data/movies

When the user sets it to /mnt/media/movies, the Hub's per-app override gets the bind mount "/mnt/media/movies:/data/movies".

items.title: ports
items.text:
Host port bindings the app needs (for non-HTTP protocols such as DNS or TURN; HTTP always goes through Traefik). The Hub:

  1. Refuses to enable the app if one of its ports is already claimed by another enabled app.
  2. Shows each port as an editable field, so users can rebind it or (if not required) disable it.
  3. Writes the effective bindings into the per-app compose override. compose.yml must not publish these ports itself.
Field Type Required Description key env key Yes Variable holding the user-overridable host port label single line, non-empty Yes UI label, e.g. DNS (TCP) protocol tcp or udp Yes service service Yes Compose service the port belongs to container integer 1–65535 Yes, unless range is set Container-side port default integer 1–65535 Yes, unless range is set Default host port range "low-high" No Inclusive port range, e.g. "49152-65535". Mutually exclusive with container and default; can't be rebound bind IPv4 or IPv6 address No Default bind address (default 0.0.0.0) required boolean No If not true, the user can clear the host port to disable the binding description string No Help text network_mode_host boolean No The service uses network_mode: host. Ports are claimed globally and can't be rebound 
ports:
  - key: ADGUARD_DNS_TCP_HOST
    label: DNS (TCP)
    container: 53
    protocol: tcp
    default: 53
    required: true
    service: adguard
  - key: COTURN_MEDIA_RANGE
    label: TURN media relays
    protocol: udp
    range: "49152-65535"
    required: true
    service: coturn
    network_mode_host: true

items.title: env
items.text:
Per-app environment variables.

Field Type Required Description key env key Yes Variable name description non-empty string Yes What it is for generate random, none or "" No random: the Hub generates 32 hex characters on first enable and writes them to the per-app .env required boolean No The variable must have a value

Secrets (passwords, OIDC client secrets, app keys) must be generate: random entries. Never hard-code a secret in compose.yml. A variable that compose.yml references as required (${VAR:?...}) must be an env entry with generate: random, because that is all the Hub writes.

env:
  - key: VAULTWARDEN_ADMIN_TOKEN
    description: Vaultwarden admin panel token
    generate: random
  - key: VAULTWARDEN_OIDC_SECRET
    description: Vaultwarden OIDC client secret
    generate: random

items.title: keycloak_clients
items.text:
OIDC clients the Hub registers in Keycloak when the app is enabled. Required (at least one) for native-oidc.

Field Type Required Description client_id ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,63}$ Yes Keycloak client ID. Core clients such as portcullis-forward-auth are reserved secret_env env key Yes The env entry (with generate: random) holding the client secret name single line, non-empty Yes Display name in Keycloak redirect_uri URI Exactly one of the two A single redirect URI redirect_uris list of URIs (at least one) Exactly one of the two Several redirect URIs email_verified_claim boolean No (default true) false: the client gets the email-unverified scope instead of email, so tokens carry email but no email_verified claim. For apps that refuse email_verified=false but accept the claim being absent (Vaultwarden). The app must then not request the email scope

Redirect URIs must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*://\S+$, so custom schemes such as app.immich:///oauth-callback work. {{DOMAIN}} is replaced.

The Hub tags each client with the template that owns it, and attaches the acr and groups scopes (see Hub → Keycloak clients).

email_verified_claim. Keycloak never trusts the LLDAP email (users can edit it), so the built-in email scope always sends email_verified: false. Some apps refuse that value. With email_verified_claim: false the Hub attaches core's email-unverified scope instead (the email claim only) and removes email from the client. Keycloak rejects a request for a scope the client doesn't have (invalid_scope), so drop email from the scopes the app requests; tests/validate.py checks *SCOPE* environment variables. The email is still unverified: identity stays sub / preferred_username, and the app must never link accounts by email (contract §8).

keycloak_clients:
  - client_id: vaultwarden
    secret_env: VAULTWARDEN_OIDC_SECRET
    redirect_uri: "https://passwords.{{DOMAIN}}/identity/connect/oidc-signin"
    name: Vaultwarden
    email_verified_claim: false

keycloak_clients:
  - client_id: immich
    secret_env: IMMICH_OIDC_SECRET
    redirect_uris:
      - "https://photos.{{DOMAIN}}/auth/login"
      - "https://photos.{{DOMAIN}}/user-settings"
      - "app.immich:///oauth-callback"
    name: Immich

items.title: config_files
items.text:
Files the Hub copies from the template directory into the core checkout when the app is enabled.

Field Type Required Description src relative path, no .. segment, no whitespace Yes Path relative to the template directory. Must exist (validate.py) dest non-empty, no .. segment Yes Destination relative to the core checkout. Must stay inside it and not at its top level

The Hub already copies the whole template directory to <core>/templates/<app-id>/ before every compose up. Mounting ./templates/<app-id>/<file> is usually all you need, and every built-in template uses config_files: [].

items.title: urls
items.text:
Links shown in the Hub.

Field Type Required Description label single line, non-empty Yes Link text url ^https?://\S+$ Yes URL, with {{DOMAIN}} replaced 
urls:
  - label: Vault
    url: "https://passwords.{{DOMAIN}}"

items.title: Validation
items.text:
Run the validator from the templates repo:

python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r tests/requirements.txt
.venv/bin/python tests/validate.py            # all templates
.venv/bin/python tests/validate.py my-app     # one template (cross-template checks still run)
.venv/bin/python tests/validate.py --strict   # warnings fail too

It prints one line per problem with a hint. Exit codes: 0 OK, 1 rule violations, 2 usage or setup error. Besides the schema, it checks:

Layout

  • the directory name is a valid app ID (^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$)
  • the files are named exactly manifest.yaml and compose.yml
  • tests/apps/<app-id>.sh exists
  • the directory is listed in .github/dependabot.yml
  • .core-ref holds exactly one ref

Manifest

  • no key is declared twice across env, settings and ports, and none shadows a core variable
  • every secret_env is an env entry with generate: random
  • port bind values are IPs and range values are valid
  • config_files sources exist
  • auth.native_login only with method: custom and sso: false, and a custom app with group_access: true declares it

Networks and volumes

  • Traefik-routed services use networks: [default, portcullis-proxy], and internal services stay off portcullis-proxy
  • portcullis-proxy is declared external: true, and no other networks are used
  • volumes declare name: portcullis_<volume>, unique across templates and never external

Variables

  • core variables use their default form, e.g. ${PORTCULLIS_TRAEFIK_IP:-172.31.250.2}
  • every other variable is declared in the manifest
  • required ${VAR:?} variables are generate: random env entries

Services

  • no ports:, build:, container_name: or env_file:
  • every image is pinned tag@sha256:digest, and floating tags (latest, 16-alpine, ...) are rejected

Bind mounts

  • only ./templates/<app-id>/<file> (the file must exist) and ./certs/ca-bundle.crt:<path>:ro
  • never ./scripts/ or another template's files

Routers

  • every router has a rule of the form Host(`<sub>.${PORTCULLIS_DOMAIN:-portcullis.local}`), and no core subdomain
  • entrypoints: websecure, and tls.options one of authaware@file, public@file, protected@file (mtls apps need protected@file)
  • security-headers@file is in the middlewares
  • portcullis-auth@docker and portcullis-groups@docker always appear together, in that order
  • forward-auth and header-auth routers use them; native-OIDC host-wide routers don't
  • public, custom and mtls routers use neither (for custom apps the Hub adds them, see auth.native_login)
  • each admin_paths entry is served by a gated router

Public exceptions (auth.public_access)

  • only for forward-auth, header-auth and native-oidc; header-auth apps list identity_headers, and every identity-like X-…/Remote-… header in compose.yml must be among them
  • the prefix, broad, never-public, overlap, matcher and token_pattern rules of auth.public_access
  • exact paths have a justification and no {token}; supporting prefixes don't name a file
  • no router or middleware named portcullis-public-*

Header trust

  • header-auth apps restrict identity headers to Traefik's IP
  • nothing trusts **, 0.0.0.0/0, ::/0 or the proxy subnet

Cross-template

  • no subdomain or volume name is used by two templates

items.title: Complete example
items.text:
A native-OIDC app with path settings, generated secrets and a Keycloak client:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=../schema/manifest.schema.json
name: Jellyfin
description: Free and open-source media server -- movies, TV, music, live TV
icon: "\U0001F4FA"
category: media
tags: [media, movies, tv, music, streaming, opensource]

auth:
  method: native-oidc
  sso: true
  group_access: true
  group_admin: true
  access_group: users_jellyfin
  admin_group: admin_jellyfin
  notes: >
    SSO-Auth plugin with group enforcement. Users must be in access_group
    to log in. Members of admin_group get Jellyfin admin.

settings:
  - key: JELLYFIN_MOVIES_PATH
    label: Movies folder
    description: Host path to your movies library
    type: path
    target:
      service: jellyfin
      mount: /data/movies

env:
  - key: JELLYFIN_ADMIN_PASSWORD
    description: Jellyfin admin password
    generate: random
  - key: JELLYFIN_OIDC_SECRET
    description: Jellyfin OIDC client secret
    generate: random

keycloak_clients:
  - client_id: jellyfin
    secret_env: JELLYFIN_OIDC_SECRET
    redirect_uris:
      - "https://media.{{DOMAIN}}/sso/OID/redirect/keycloak"
    name: Jellyfin

config_files: []

urls:
  - label: Jellyfin
    url: "https://media.{{DOMAIN}}"

A forward-auth app with host ports:

name: Pi-hole
description: Network-wide ad blocking via DNS sinkhole
icon: "\U0001F6AB"
category: networking
tags: [dns, adblock, privacy, filtering]

auth:
  method: forward-auth
  sso: false
  group_access: true
  group_admin: false
  access_group: users_pihole
  admin_group: admin_pihole
  notes: No SSO support. Has its own web password. Access gated by group-gate middleware.

ports:
  - key: PIHOLE_DNS_TCP_HOST
    label: DNS (TCP)
    container: 53
    protocol: tcp
    default: 53
    required: true
    service: pihole
  - key: PIHOLE_DNS_UDP_HOST
    label: DNS (UDP)
    container: 53
    protocol: udp
    default: 53
    required: true
    service: pihole

env:
  - key: PIHOLE_WEBPASSWORD
    description: Pi-hole web interface password
    generate: random

keycloak_clients: []
config_files: []

urls:
  - label: Dashboard
    url: "https://pihole.{{DOMAIN}}/admin"

The real manifests of every built-in template are rendered in the App Catalog.

items.title: SAML Integration
items.text: This guide shows how to integrate a SAML-capable application with Portcullis, using Nextcloud as a worked example. The same pattern applies to any app that supports SAML 2.0.

items.title: Overview
items.text:
User (YubiKey) --> Traefik --> App
                                |
                                v  SAML SSO
                             Keycloak (IdP)
                                |
                                v  user lookup
                              LLDAP

The user authenticates at the Traefik layer (via mTLS or WebAuthn). The app then uses SAML to verify the user's identity via Keycloak, which looks up users in LLDAP.

items.title: Step 1: Deploy the App
items.text:
Create a Docker Compose file for the app (or use its template from the catalog). The key Traefik labels are:

services:
  nextcloud:
    image: nextcloud:<version>-apache@sha256:<digest>   # pin tag + digest
    environment:
      NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_USER: admin
      NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_PASSWORD:?generated}   # never ship a default password
      NEXTCLOUD_TRUSTED_DOMAINS: "nextcloud.${PORTCULLIS_DOMAIN}"
    networks:
      - default
      - portcullis-proxy
    labels:
      traefik.enable: "true"
      traefik.http.routers.nextcloud.rule: "Host(`nextcloud.${PORTCULLIS_DOMAIN}`)"
      traefik.http.routers.nextcloud.entrypoints: websecure
      traefik.http.routers.nextcloud.tls.options: authaware@file
      traefik.http.routers.nextcloud.middlewares: security-headers@file
      traefik.http.services.nextcloud.loadbalancer.server.port: "80"

networks:
  portcullis-proxy:
    external: true

Apps join portcullis-proxy (shared with Traefik), never the core portcullis network.

Note: SAML apps handle their own authentication flow with Keycloak, so they do not need the portcullis-auth@docker forward-auth middleware.

items.title: Step 2: Register the App as a SAML Client in Keycloak
2a. Open Keycloak Admin
items.text: Navigate to https://auth.<your-domain>/admin/ and sign in with your passkey as a member of lldap_admin (the realm admins of the portcullis realm). Select the portcullis realm from the dropdown.

items.title: 2b. Create a New SAML Client
items.text:
1. Navigate to Clients and click Create client
  2. Set:
  3. Client type: SAML
  4. Client ID: https://nextcloud.<your-domain>/apps/user_saml/saml/metadata
  5. Click Next
  6. On the next screen:
  7. Name: Nextcloud
  8. Root URL: https://nextcloud.<your-domain>
  9. Valid redirect URIs: https://nextcloud.<your-domain>/*
  10. Click Save

items.title: 2c. Configure SAML Settings
items.text:
In the client settings, go to the Settings tab:

  • Name ID format: username
  • Force name ID format: ON
  • Sign assertions: ON
  • Signature algorithm: RSA_SHA256
  • SAML signature key name: KEY_ID

Go to the Keys tab:

  • Client signature required: OFF (unless the app is configured to sign requests)

items.title: 2d. Add Attribute Mappers
items.text:
Go to Client scopes, click the client's dedicated scope, then Add mapper and select By configuration:

Email mapper:

  • Mapper type: User Property
  • Name: email
  • Property: email
  • SAML Attribute Name: urn:oid:0.9.2342.19200300.100.1.3
  • SAML Attribute NameFormat: URI Reference

Username mapper:

  • Mapper type: User Property
  • Name: username
  • Property: username
  • SAML Attribute Name: urn:oid:0.9.2342.19200300.100.1.1
  • SAML Attribute NameFormat: URI Reference

Display name mapper:

  • Mapper type: User Property
  • Name: displayName
  • Property: firstName
  • SAML Attribute Name: urn:oid:2.16.840.1.113730.3.1.241
  • SAML Attribute NameFormat: URI Reference

items.title: 2e. Note the IdP Metadata URL
items.text:
You will need this when configuring the app:

https://auth.<your-domain>/realms/portcullis/protocol/saml/descriptor

items.title: Step 3: Configure the App for SAML
items.text: This section uses Nextcloud as an example. Adapt the field names for your specific app.

items.title: 3a. Enable the SAML Plugin
items.text:
In Nextcloud, enable the SSO & SAML authentication app:

docker compose exec nextcloud php occ app:enable user_saml

items.title: 3b. Configure SAML Settings
items.text:
In Nextcloud's Administration settings under SSO & SAML authentication:

General:

  • Attribute to map the UID to: urn:oid:0.9.2342.19200300.100.1.1

Identity Provider Data:

  • Identifier of the IdP entity: https://auth.<your-domain>/realms/portcullis
  • URL target of the IdP where the SP will send the Authentication Request: https://auth.<your-domain>/realms/portcullis/protocol/saml
  • URL Location of IdP where the SP will send the SLO Request: https://auth.<your-domain>/realms/portcullis/protocol/saml
  • Public X.509 certificate of the IdP: Download from the SAML descriptor URL (Step 2e), extract the <ds:X509Certificate> value, and paste it

Service Provider Data:

  • Identifier of the SP entity: https://nextcloud.<your-domain>/apps/user_saml/saml/metadata

Attribute mapping:

  • Attribute to map the displayname to: urn:oid:2.16.840.1.113730.3.1.241
  • Attribute to map the email address to: urn:oid:0.9.2342.19200300.100.1.3

items.title: 3c. Test SAML Login
items.text:
1. Open a private/incognito window
  2. Go to https://nextcloud.<your-domain>
  3. You should see a "Login with SSO" button or be redirected automatically
  4. Keycloak authenticates with your passkey (or client certificate if mTLS is enabled)
  5. You are logged into the app

items.title: Step 4: Optional -- LDAP User Backend
items.text:
For richer user integration (groups, quotas, etc.), you can also configure the app's LDAP backend to read from LLDAP directly:

Setting Value Host lldap (Docker service name) Port 3890 User DN uid=admin,ou=people,<your-base-dn> Password Your LLDAP admin password Base DN Your LLDAP_BASE_DN value User object class person Username attribute uid Email attribute mail Group object class groupOfUniqueNames

This way, users and groups from LLDAP appear directly in the app, while SAML handles the authentication flow.

items.title: General SAML Pattern
items.text:
The same steps apply to any SAML-capable application:

  1. Deploy the app behind Traefik (no forward-auth middleware needed)
  2. Create a SAML client in Keycloak with the app's entity ID and ACS URL
  3. Configure attribute mappers for email, username, and display name
  4. Point the app's SAML settings at Keycloak's IdP metadata
  5. Test the SSO flow

items.title: "Invalid signature" on SAML response
items.text:
• Ensure the IdP certificate in the app matches the one from Keycloak's SAML descriptor
  • Check that "Sign assertions" is ON in the Keycloak client config

items.title: User not found after SAML login
items.text:
• Verify the UID attribute mapping matches between Keycloak and the app
  • Check that the user exists in LLDAP and has synced to Keycloak (Keycloak admin panel, Users, search for the username)

items.title: SAML loop / redirect issues
items.text:
• Ensure the app's trusted domains configuration includes your full domain
  • Check that the entity ID in Keycloak matches exactly what the app sends
  • Verify the ACS URL is correct in Keycloak's Valid Redirect URIs

items.title: Mixed content / proxy issues
items.text:
For apps behind a reverse proxy, you typically need to configure the app to know it is behind HTTPS. For Nextcloud, add to config.php:

'overwriteprotocol' => 'https',
'overwrite.cli.url' => 'https://nextcloud.<your-domain>',
'trusted_proxies' => ['172.31.250.2'],   // PORTCULLIS_TRAEFIK_IP only

Trust only Traefik's fixed address (PORTCULLIS_TRAEFIK_IP, default 172.31.250.2), never whole private ranges: every app container on portcullis-proxy could otherwise set its own X-Forwarded-For.

Other apps have similar settings (e.g., FORCE_HTTPS, TRUST_PROXY, SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER).

items.title: Third-Party Apps
items.text:
This guide explains how to put existing Docker apps behind Portcullis authentication without creating a Hub template. Use this when you have an app that:

  • Is already running (or you manage its compose file yourself)
  • Doesn't need to appear in the Hub catalog
  • Just needs to be reachable through Portcullis with SSO/group enforcement

items.title: Quick Overview
items.text: Any Docker container can join the portcullis-proxy network and get Traefik routing + authentication by adding the right labels. No manifest, no Hub, no template repo required.

items.title: Option 1: Forward Auth (app has no SSO support)
items.text: Best for apps that have no OIDC/SAML support — Portcullis handles authentication entirely.

items.title: compose.yml
items.text:
services:
  myapp:
    image: myorg/myapp:latest
    networks:
      - default
      - portcullis-proxy
    labels:
      traefik.enable: "true"
      traefik.http.routers.myapp.rule: Host(`myapp.${PORTCULLIS_DOMAIN}`)
      traefik.http.routers.myapp.entrypoints: websecure
      traefik.http.routers.myapp.tls.options: authaware@file
      traefik.http.routers.myapp.middlewares: client-headers@file,portcullis-auth@docker,portcullis-groups@docker,security-headers@file
      traefik.http.services.myapp.loadbalancer.server.port: "8080"
    restart: unless-stopped

networks:
  portcullis-proxy:
    external: true

items.title: What this does
items.text:
1. User visits https://myapp.yourdomain.com
  2. portcullis-auth@docker (oauth2-proxy) checks for a session cookie
  3. No cookie → redirect to Keycloak → user authenticates with YubiKey
  4. portcullis-groups@docker (group-gate) checks the user's groups
  5. If authorized → request forwarded to your app

items.title: Group enforcement
items.text:
Add your app's subdomain to group-gate/group-gate-map.conf in the core checkout:

myapp=users_myapp

Then create the group in LLDAP and add users to it. group-gate re-reads the map file on every request, so no restart is needed. If you skip this step, any authenticated Portcullis user can access the app (group-gate logs ALLOW-UNMAPPED).

Use a subdomain no Hub app uses

group-gate keys everything by subdomain. If a Hub-enabled app routes the same subdomain, the Hub's groups entry overrides the map file. Hosts outside <label>.<PORTCULLIS_DOMAIN> are always denied by group-gate. Core subdomains (auth, traefik, hub, directory, enroll, metrics) cannot be reused.

client-headers@file must come before portcullis-groups@docker, so group-gate sees the client certificate and can enforce revocation. For admin-only paths, use a separate PathPrefix router; per-path groups (path_groups) are only published by the Hub for templates.

items.title: Passing user identity
items.text:
The authenticated user's LLDAP username is available to your app in the X-Forwarded-User header (set by the group-gate middleware), the email in X-Forwarded-Email and the groups in X-Auth-Request-Groups. Identify users by the username: LLDAP users can edit their own email. Many apps support "trusted header" authentication.

Trust the header only from Traefik

Every container on portcullis-proxy can connect to your app directly. Configure the app to accept identity headers only from PORTCULLIS_TRAEFIK_IP (default 172.31.250.2), never from the whole subnet. See Header Auth Pattern → Header Security.

App Framework Config Grafana GF_AUTH_PROXY_ENABLED=true, GF_AUTH_PROXY_HEADER_NAME=X-Forwarded-User, GF_AUTH_PROXY_HEADER_PROPERTY=username, GF_AUTH_PROXY_WHITELIST=172.31.250.2 Kanboard REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH=true, REVERSE_PROXY_USER_HEADER=HTTP_X_FORWARDED_USER, TRUSTED_PROXY_NETWORKS=172.31.250.2/32 Firefly III AUTHENTICATION_GUARD=remote_user_guard Generic Read X-Forwarded-User header in your app

items.title: Option 2: Native OIDC (app supports OpenID Connect)
items.text: Best for apps that have built-in OIDC/OAuth2 support. The app handles its own login flow with Keycloak.

items.title: Step 1: Register a Keycloak client
items.text:
# Get admin token
TOKEN=$(curl -s http://localhost:8080/realms/master/protocol/openid-connect/token \
  -d "client_id=admin-cli" \
  -d "username=admin" \
  -d "password=$KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD" \
  -d "grant_type=password" | jq -r '.access_token')

# Register client
curl -s http://localhost:8080/admin/realms/portcullis/clients \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "clientId": "myapp",
    "enabled": true,
    "protocol": "openid-connect",
    "publicClient": false,
    "secret": "your-client-secret-here",
    "redirectUris": ["https://myapp.yourdomain.com/callback"],
    "standardFlowEnabled": true,
    "directAccessGrantsEnabled": false,
    "defaultClientScopes": ["openid", "profile", "email", "acr", "groups"]
  }'

items.title: Step 2: Configure your app
items.text:
Point your app's OIDC settings to:

Setting Value Issuer / Authority https://auth.yourdomain.com/realms/portcullis Discovery URL https://auth.yourdomain.com/realms/portcullis/.well-known/openid-configuration Client ID myapp Client Secret your-client-secret-here Scopes openid email profile groups Redirect URI https://myapp.yourdomain.com/callback

items.title: Step 3: compose.yml
items.text:
Native OIDC apps don't need portcullis-auth@docker — they handle auth themselves:

services:
  myapp:
    image: myorg/myapp:latest
    environment:
      OIDC_ISSUER: https://auth.${PORTCULLIS_DOMAIN}/realms/portcullis
      OIDC_CLIENT_ID: myapp
      OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET: your-client-secret-here
    networks:
      - default
      - portcullis-proxy
    labels:
      traefik.enable: "true"
      traefik.http.routers.myapp.rule: Host(`myapp.${PORTCULLIS_DOMAIN}`)
      traefik.http.routers.myapp.entrypoints: websecure
      traefik.http.routers.myapp.tls.options: authaware@file
      traefik.http.routers.myapp.middlewares: client-headers@file,security-headers@file
      traefik.http.services.myapp.loadbalancer.server.port: "8080"
    restart: unless-stopped

networks:
  portcullis-proxy:
    external: true

No portcullis-auth@docker middleware

Native OIDC apps handle their own auth flow. Don't add portcullis-auth@docker or portcullis-groups@docker — the app redirects to Keycloak itself.

items.title: Staging certificates
items.text:
If you're using Let's Encrypt staging (ACME_STAGING=true), your app needs to trust the staging CA. Mount the CA bundle:

services:
  myapp:
    volumes:
      - /path/to/portcullis/certs/ca-bundle.crt:/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt:ro
    environment:
      # For Node.js apps:
      NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS: /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
      # For Go apps:
      SSL_CERT_FILE: /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt

items.title: Option 3: Public (no authentication)
items.text:
For apps that should be publicly accessible:

services:
  myapp:
    image: myorg/myapp:latest
    networks:
      - default
      - portcullis-proxy
    labels:
      traefik.enable: "true"
      traefik.http.routers.myapp.rule: Host(`myapp.${PORTCULLIS_DOMAIN}`)
      traefik.http.routers.myapp.entrypoints: websecure
      traefik.http.routers.myapp.tls.options: public@file
      traefik.http.routers.myapp.middlewares: security-headers@file
      traefik.http.services.myapp.loadbalancer.server.port: "8080"
    restart: unless-stopped

networks:
  portcullis-proxy:
    external: true

Note: tls.options: public@file (no client cert request) and no auth middleware.

items.title: Running Alongside Portcullis
items.text:
Start your app with its own project name to keep it isolated:

docker compose -p myapp -f /path/to/your/compose.yml up -d

Your app gets its own containers, network, and lifecycle — completely independent of the Portcullis core stack.

items.title: Comparison: Template vs Third-Party
items.text:
Feature Hub Template Third-Party Appears in Hub catalog Yes No One-click enable/disable Yes Manual compose up/down Auto-generated secrets Yes Manual Per-app settings UI Yes Edit compose/env directly Status/logs in Hub Yes docker compose logs Keycloak client auto-registration Yes Manual registration Group-gate mapping Via manifest (access_group, admin_paths) Edit group-gate/group-gate-map.conf Auth badges in UI Yes N/A

For apps you manage frequently or share with others, consider creating a proper template. For one-off apps or quick experiments, the third-party approach is simpler.

items.title: Authentication Policies
items.text: Portcullis lets you require either or both of two hardware-backed factors (a passkey, a client certificate) for each app, with AND or OR semantics, plus a global default. Each app enforces only what its auth method can (see What each app can enforce). This page explains the model and how to use it.

items.title: Factors
items.text:
Factor How the user proves it Keycloak executor amr value LoA WebAuthn Taps a hardware security key (YubiKey, platform authenticator) webauthn-authenticator-passwordless hwk 2 mTLS Presents a client certificate over TLS (PIV / YubiKey cert) auth-x509-client-username-form mtls 3

LoA = Level of Authentication, a number Keycloak uses for step-up. Every sign-in is a passkey or a client cert and reaches LoA 2 in one touch (oauth2-proxy asks for hwk by default); LoA 3 needs the cert. First passkeys come from one-time setup links (./portcullis invite, the Hub's Users & Groups).

There is no password factor

The realm's browser flow has no password: its LoA 1 (pwd) subflow is a client cert or a passkey, the same as LoA 2. The Hub never offers or writes password, and its API refuses it (400). A stored policy that still names it is normalised when the Hub loads state.yaml, never into something weaker: in an all policy it is redundant and dropped; as an alternative (any, or alone) it accepted every session, so it becomes any of [mtls, webauthn]. The app's settings (or the Settings tab) show a note until the policy is saved. group-gate still parses password (met by every hwk/mtls session) but the Hub no longer publishes it.

items.title: Policy model
items.text:
A policy has two parts:

  1. Factors — zero or more of mtls, webauthn.
  2. Op — any (any selected factor satisfies the policy) or all (every selected factor must have fired in the current session).

Special cases:

  • Zero factors → public (no authentication required).
  • One factor → the single factor is required; op is ignored.

Examples:

Policy Meaning {factors: [], op: ""} Public {factors: ["webauthn"]} A passkey {factors: ["mtls", "webauthn"], op: "any"} Either mTLS or WebAuthn {factors: ["mtls", "webauthn"], op: "all"} mTLS and WebAuthn (both must fire)

items.title: In the Hub UI
items.text:
Per-app — open an app in the catalog and use the Access policy block above the settings form:

  • Every app starts with Inherit global default ticked. While it inherits, the factor boxes are disabled and show the app's effective policy: the global default intersected with what the app can enforce, with a note when the two differ (e.g. "The global default allows mTLS or WebAuthn; this app can't enforce WebAuthn, so it enforces mTLS").
  • Untick Inherit to set an override. Only factors the app can enforce are selectable; the others are greyed out ("this app can't enforce it"), and the Hub refuses them with a 400 too.
  • If two or more are ticked, pick Require all checked (AND) or Any of checked (OR).
  • Apps that handle their own sign-in (custom, public, or an app switched to its own login only) show the block disabled: "This app handles its own sign-in".

Global default — the Settings tab exposes the default policy that every app without an override uses. Changing it affects all apps whose per-app policy is unset.

Fresh installs require a YubiKey

Until an admin saves a global default, the Hub uses any of [mtls, webauthn] ({"factors": ["mtls", "webauthn"], "op": "any"}). Every app without its own policy then requires the YubiKey, by either method: its client certificate (mtls, LoA 3) or a passkey (webauthn, LoA 2).

  • Routers get authaware@file: the certificate is optional at the handshake.
  • Keycloak steps up to at least LoA 2 (hwk).
  • group-gate accepts mtls or hwk in amr, so a certificate sign-in passes too (including enroll.<domain>/self renewal).
  • A password-only session gets the step-up page.

A WebAuthn-only default would send certificate users to the step-up page on every app. An explicitly saved public default is stored and honoured. It is not the same as "never set".

The safety score next to each policy is a cosmetic sum: 0 for public, LoA for a single factor, LoA + 0.5 per extra required factor for AND policies.

items.title: What each app can enforce
items.text:
Auth method Factors Where forward-auth, header-auth, custom behind Portcullis sign-in mtls, webauthn group-gate, on every request; a certificate is bound to the user (mTLS binding) native-oidc mtls, webauthn Keycloak, when the user signs in to the app (acr of its client). mTLS is checked per connection only when the policy selects the protected@file tier (mTLS alone, or all including it) mtls mtls The TLS handshake (protected@file), always: the certificate stays required even under a public or WebAuthn-only default, and an override can only be [mtls] custom, public, own login only none The app handles its own sign-in; no policy, tier public@file

The effective policy is the configured one (override or global default) with the unsupported factors left out. For any that removes an alternative; for all it removes a requirement the app can't check, which the app's settings say. If nothing of the configured policy is enforceable (a WebAuthn-only default on an mTLS-only app), the app's own floor applies (the certificate) and the settings say so. The TLS tier and the Keycloak acr come from the effective policy. The policy file is unchanged: overrides are published as stored (they only name supported factors), inheriting apps publish nothing.

items.title: Apps with their own login
items.text:
A custom template whose app has its own login and no SSO declares auth.native_login. Its settings then have a Sign-in choice:

  • Portcullis sign-in, then the app's own login (default). The Hub's override puts portcullis-auth@docker,portcullis-groups@docker in front of every router's own middlewares; group-gate requires the template's access_group and the policy applies per request, as for forward-auth.
  • App's own login only (no Portcullis), only if the template sets allow_without_gateway: true. The routers keep the template's middlewares without the gateway pair, the tier is public@file and no group is published: anyone on the internet reaches the app's login page. The UI shows a red warning, the switch is audited (app.sign_in) and the Hub logs it.

The template is never edited; both modes are compose-override labels, which the drift check compares with the running containers. If a template stops allowing the own-login-only mode, the Hub falls back to Portcullis sign-in.

items.title: What happens when a user hits an app
Same-LoA SSO (no step-up)
items.text: User signs in to Grafana with a passkey (policy: any of [mtls, webauthn], session acr=hwk). Opens Immich (policy: webauthn). The Keycloak session already satisfies the required LoA, so Immich gets a token with no further prompt. Same for any other apps with policies their session already satisfies.

items.title: Step-up on a stricter app
items.text: User signed in with a passkey (amr=[hwk], LoA 2). Opens Jellyfin with policy mtls-required. Keycloak sees the session's current LoA is 2, but Jellyfin's client requested acr_values=mtls (LoA 3). The Condition - Level of Authentication executor in the universal flow fires only the mTLS subflow — the certificate is asked for, nothing else. On success the session's LoA is upgraded to 3 and amr becomes [hwk, mtls]. No full re-login.

items.title: Step-up on forward-auth apps
items.text: oauth2-proxy ≥ 7.10 accepts per-request acr_values via the loginURLParameters alpha-config setting, which is what Portcullis runs (allowed values pwd, hwk, mtls; default hwk; kc_idp_hint=portcullis-invite and prompt=login exist only for setup links). When group-gate detects a session that doesn't satisfy the app's policy, it returns a 403 "Additional authentication required" page with the URL in an X-Stepup-URL header: https://auth.<domain>/oauth2/start?acr_values=<needed>&rd=https://<app>/. The step-up always goes through auth.<domain>; there is no /oauth2/ router on app hosts. There is no sign-out and no prompt=login: Keycloak's cookie authenticator runs the flow when the requested LoA is above the session's and asks only for the missing level. The new token reflects the step-up. When the missing factor is a hardware one (passkey / cert) the page does not auto-redirect: a Continue button, and links to register a passkey in the account console or enrol a certificate at enroll.<domain>. Other step-ups redirect after 2 seconds.

items.title: Public policy
